title: Rav Chama son of Rabbah bar Avuha
author: Aharon Hyman
attribution: Model-assisted translation, editorially reviewed; publication authorized by Joshua Waxman.

paragraphs: He was like a colleague of Abaye, as in Eruvin 3a, where Abaye raised a difficulty against Rav Yosef: “But Chama son of Rabbah bar Avuha teaches it.” In Bava Metzia 105b a certain elder said to him, “I will explain it to you.”

Hyman infers that he went to the Land of Israel and afterward returned to Babylonia, as in Ketubot 85a: Avimi son of Rabbi Abbahu — the people of Bei Chozai had a claim of money against him (that is, they were his creditors); he sent it through Chama son of Rava bar Abbahu. He went and paid them; he said to them, “Give me the document.” They said to him, “These are for another debt.” (Avimi — so it is in the Rif) came before Rabbi Abbahu, etc.

notes.text: Avimi owed money to the people of Bei Chozai and sent repayment through Chama. Chama asks for the debt document; the creditors claim the money covers another debt, not receipts. Saved Davidson Ketubot 85a confirms that direction. The supplied body writes Rava bar Abbahu, while the heading has Rabbah bar Avuha; that variant is now preserved instead of silently harmonized. Hyman’s travel inference remains attributed.

Avimi owed the money and sent payment through Chama; the creditors claimed it paid a different debt. The heading’s Rabbah bar Avuha and the body’s Rava bar Abbahu are preserved. The journey inference and the report of the Rif reading remain attributed to Hyman.
